cards.explanation: The answer is the desires of the flesh. Paul says, "So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh." Notice the order, friends. The walking by the Spirit comes first, and the not gratifying comes with it. Paul doesn't hand over a list of things to white-knuckle your way past first.

The answer is True. Paul says the flesh and the Spirit "…are opposed to each other, so that you do not do what you want." I know this feeling, friends. I can plan to eat one cookie off the cooling rack, and the plan and I are not always on the same page. Paul is describing a real pull in two directions.

The answer is False. Paul says, "But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law." So being under the law is the opposite of what he says, friends. Being led by the Spirit and being under the law are not the same thing.

The answer is False. Paul says, "The acts of the flesh are obvious…" so he isn't saying they're hidden or hard to spot. He then names them one by one, friends. That's a heavy list, and he treats it plainly.

The answer is that they will not inherit the kingdom of God. Paul says, "I warn you, as I did before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God." He had already told them this before, and he says it again, friends. It's a serious line, so I'll let it stand there quietly.

The answer is patience, friends. Paul writes, "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control." Patience is fourth of the nine. I'll admit it's the one I practiced the most staring at a closed oven door.

The answer is True. Right after the fruit, Paul says, "Against such things there is no law." Nobody is going to hand you a ticket for too much kindness, friends. Love, joy, peace and the rest are free and clear.

The answer is crucified, friends. Paul says, "Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires." He says it about everyone who belongs to Christ Jesus. It's a strong word, and it tells me those passions and desires don't get the final say for those who belong to Him.

The answer is True. Paul says, "Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit." Living by the Spirit is where he starts, friends, and walking in step follows. It's like a good dance partner: you've already said yes to the dance, so now you keep in step.

The answer is conceited. Paul writes, "Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another." Notice he says "us," friends, so he counts himself in. Even a stamper with a mustache this magnificent has to watch out for that one.
